prompt: I'm working in a repo that uses git-stack. I'm 3 commits deep on my feature branch and I just noticed the very first commit renamed a function wrong (`fetchUser` should be `getUser`). I've already fixed the file in my working tree. Walk me through correcting that earliest commit with git-stack so the two commits stacked on top of it come along cleanly. Give me the exact commands. Don't run any history-rewriting commands against my repo — just give me the plan.

assertions.text: Uses git-stack navigation (git-stack previous) to reach the earlier commit instead of copying SHAs
Uses `git-stack amend` (optionally with -a) to meld the staged fix into the target commit
Notes that git-stack automatically rebases the descendant commits onto the amended commit
Does NOT recommend `git rebase -i` / interactive rebase or `git commit --amend` + manual rebase as the primary method
